name: Febuxostat
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero

usual_adult_dose.indication: Chronic hyperuricemia in gout (allopurinol inadequate, not tolerated or inadvisable)
usual_adult_dose.dose: Start 40 mg once daily; 80 mg once daily if serum urate is not below 6 mg/dL after 2 weeks; limit to 40 mg in severe kidney impairment

key_interactions.action: No label recommendation beyond the absence of data.

common: Liver function abnormalities, nausea, arthralgia, rash (≥1%)
serious: Cardiovascular death in gout patients with established cardiovascular disease (boxed warning; higher than allopurinol in CARES)

monitoring: Serum urate (target below 6 mg/dL) from 2 weeks
Liver tests before starting and if symptoms of liver injury
Signs of myocardial infarction or stroke
Flare prophylaxis with an NSAID or colchicine when starting

pk.bioavailability: At least 49% absorbed (absolute bioavailability not studied)
pk.half_life_eskd: Not studied in ESKD; AUC up to 1.8-fold and longer half-life at CrCl 10 to 29 mL/min (label)
pk.active_metabolites: Four hydroxy metabolites (much lower plasma levels than parent)
pk.excretion_renal_pct: About 49% in urine (3% unchanged); about 45% in feces
